name: Random Equivalence Queries Complexity of Singletons
proof: Fix a counterexample distribution $\mu$ with $\mu(i)>0$ for every $i\in[n]$. For $n=1$, output the sole target without a query. For $n\ge2$, query the all-zero hypothesis. Against target $\{i\}$ the disagreement set is exactly $\{i\}$, so the random counterexample is deterministically $(i,1)$ for every allowed $\mu$. It identifies the target in one query. An exact learner cannot identify an unknown target among two or more concepts without any observation, so the worst-case expected query count is at least one. Thus the value is one, independently of $\mu$ on the stated domain.
details: For every fixed counterexample distribution $\mu$ with $\mu(i)>0$ for all $i\in[n]$.
